The Sacramento Kings are spiraling early in the season, and rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. isn’t trying to sugarcoat the frustration anymore. Sacramento hit another low point on Tuesday night, falling 107-100 to the Orlando Magic at Golden 1 Center. The defeat dropped the Kings to a dismal 1-10 record, tying the worst 11-game start in franchise history. Despite the team’s ongoing slide, Acuff put on another spectacular individual show. The 18-year-old guard led Sacramento’s attack with 29 points, six assists, and four rebounds while playing 40 minutes. But personal box-score numbers meant very little to the rookie after watching another winnable game slip away in front of the home crowd. Following the loss, beat reporter Frankie Cartoscelli posted on X that Acuff was visibly frustrated while addressing the media. The rookie guard held nothing back when assessing Sacramento’s struggles. When the clock hits zero and we’re losing, that’s the most frustrating part.”Acuff has shouldered a massive load early, becoming the first NBA rookie since 1983 to attempt at least 20 shots in each of his first 10 career games. He got offensive support from veteran guard Zach LaVine, but Sacramento couldn’t string together enough late stops. Orlando executed key possessions down the stretch, keeping the Kings winless at home with an 0-6 mark. Sacramento’s locker room communication has yet to pay dividends on the court. While Acuff continues to show superstar potential, high-scoring nights won’t soften the blow for a rookie driven by winning. Until the Kings fix their late-game execution, the frustration in Sacramento will only build. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’
item.description: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’ Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha has credited Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal with changing the way young footballers approach the game, describing the teenager as one of the best players in the world. Speaking in an interview with The Independent , the 18-year-old England international highlighted how Yamal’s confidence, freedom and performances at such a young age have inspired the next generation. Ngumoha’s comments come ahead of England’s November Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain. Thomas Tuchel has included the Liverpool winger in his squad following his encouraging performances at club level, potentially giving him an opportunity to face the Barcelona star when England meet Spain. Ngumoha sees Yamal as an inspiration for young players Speaking during a lengthy interview, Ngumoha did not hide his admiration when asked about the Barcelona winger, whose development has established him among the leading young talents in European football. Rio Ngumoha sees Lamine Yamal as an inspiration. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) “I think what he’s doing has changed football for young players. He’s extraordinary. He’s one of the best in the world,” said Ngumoha when asked about the Barcelona star. The Liverpool forward believes Yamal’s performances show that young footballers should not be afraid to express themselves or take responsibility on the pitch. Rather than allowing their age to restrict their ambitions, they can use his example as encouragement to play with confidence. “Seeing what he can do at such a young age inspires me and all the other young players to play freely. “He plays as if the pitch were his own. It’s a great challenge,” noted the Reds’ forward. England call-up pit Ngumoha against Yamal Rio Ngumoha could come up against Yamal later this month. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Ngumoha’s admiration for Yamal could soon become a personal challenge. This is because England are scheduled to face Croatia on November 12 before travelling to Spain on November 15 at the Metropolitano, with the latter fixture potentially bringing the two young wingers onto the same pitch. At 18, Ngumoha is the youngest player in Tuchel’s November England squad and has already made his senior international debut. Yamal, on the other hand, is an established member of Barcelona and Spain’s setup, and a meeting with the Spaniard would offer Ngumoha an opportunity to test himself against a player whose development he clearly admires.

item.title: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes
item.description: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes Aimar Blázquez scored twice from Rioja assists as Valencia beat Tavernes 6-0 at Mestalla, where the hosts were officially the away side. The win follows a 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid and takes Valencia into the second round. Valencia cruised past Tavernes in the Copa del Rey on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The tie was played at the Estadio de Mestalla, yet Valencia were officially the away side in their own stadium. The RFEF had granted Tavernes’ request to stage the match there. Valencia were four goals up inside 23 minutes Raba opened the scoring in the first minute, with Blázquez providing the assist. Raba then turned provider for Duro in the 11th minute. Rioja added the third in the 19th minute after a pass from Martinez. A fourth goal arrived through Elliott in the 23rd minute. Tavernes goalkeeper Mainar kept the margin there three minutes into the second half. He saved a header from Blázquez, who had been set up by Raba. The number 37 struck in the 57th minute and again in the 69th. Danjuma replaced him after 70 minutes, when Gayà also came on for Rioja. Three players were booked. Ugrinic was cautioned in the ninth minute and Montilla of Tavernes in the 22nd. Rioja picked up a yellow card in the 49th minute. Tavernes came closest to a goal when Erik struck the post after a short corner. EFE described the visitors as a sixth-tier club and reported that close to 40 coaches carried their fans to Mestalla. Their municipal ground was not fit for the tie. Mestalla is in its final season before the move to Nou Mestalla. The original 9pm kick-off fell to the RFEF’s postponements A 9pm start had been planned for the tie. Every Copa del Rey match scheduled for that day was called off by the RFEF, and this one was among them. Tavernes reached the first round through the two-legged preliminary round against UD Maracena. The first leg was played at the CD Maracena ground on Sunday 27 September 2026. The two sides drew 1-1 and 0-0. For Valencia, the Real Madrid loss had itself followed a 1-0 win over Elche and a 1-2 defeat to Villarreal. Javier Aguirre said he took positive conclusions from the tie. He welcomed the return of players who had been out long-term. He also said Valencia now need to win in the league. The cup calendar continues with the round of 32 on 16 December. The last 16 follows on 6 January and the quarter-finals on 13 January. The semi-finals are the only two-legged round, with first legs on 10 February and second legs on 3 March. The competition runs until 24 April 2027. Valencia return to league action away to Rayo Vallecano at the Estadio de Vallecas on Saturday 21 November. Former Test spinner Stuart MacGill has now offered his own account of life on the field in an earlier era, and it makes for rather uncomfortable reading for those who believed the issue began and ended with one infamous afternoon. MacGill played 44 Tests for Australia between 1998 and 2008, picking up 208 wickets at an average of 29.02. He was widely regarded as one of the most prolific strike bowlers of his generation, and his career ran alongside that of the great Shane Warne. The incidents he described belong to the late 1990s and 2000s, which is well before the March 2018 episode in Cape Town that led to 12-month bans for Steve Smith and David Warner and a nine-month ban for Cameron Bancroft. item.title: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay
item.description: MLS Betting Handle Jumps 38.8% as World Cup Bettors Stay MLS has pulled in significantly more betting action in 2026 than the year before , with a 30.4% jump in tickets and a 38.8% rise in money wagered from mid-July through the end of October, according to data reported by ESPN. The surge follows a 2026 World Cup that generated $60.2 million in betting revenue in Colorado alone — a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million the 2022 tournament produced in that state. BetMGM saw a similar pattern across the broader club game: a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% jump in handle on club soccer wagers in the two months after the World Cup final. Why bettors didn't leave when the tournament ended The explanation, according to sportsbooks, is simple carryover. Hard Rock Bet SVP of sportsbook Neil Walsh told ESPN that bettors who backed Mbappé, Haaland and Kane during the World Cup followed them straight into the Champions League , and that the pattern has extended into domestic leagues as the new seasons opened. DraftKings director of sports operations Johnny Avello described the same shift on the MLS side, saying the league has seen a jump in users betting soccer, with much of that growth traced back to people who discovered the sport through World Cup wagering. That's a different dynamic than past tournaments, where interest in soccer betting typically spiked and faded once the trophy was lifted. This time, sportsbooks are describing a bettor who stuck around — treating MLS, the Champions League and the Premier League as extensions of the same summer rather than separate products to rediscover each fall. What it means for MLS's business case The timing matters. MLS is in the process of shifting to a fall-spring calendar that lines up with the rest of world soccer, a move aimed at reducing the gap between the league's rhythm and the global calendar that casual American fans already follow. A betting market that's already behaving like it expects continuity — rather than a hard reset after the World Cup — gives the league a data point to point to when it makes that case to broadcasters and sponsors. Betting handle isn't the same as television ratings or attendance, but sportsbooks track engagement in real time, and operators are reporting sustained demand rather than a one-off spike. If that holds through a full MLS season under the new calendar, it strengthens the argument that the 2026 World Cup didn't just boost a single summer — it reset how a chunk of the American betting public treats club soccer going forward.

Old Trafford power holders were certainly fully aware of the situation on Sunday, as there was a “more visible police presence in the Stretford End and stewards asking fans as they entered that section of the stadium which group they were with.” The green and gold balloon release protest was jointly organised by The Red Army, The 1958, Manchester United Youth Supporters Club, South Stand United, and Retro Reds. item.title: Confirmed: Real Madrid midfield mainstay injured in national team training; will report back to club for tests
item.description: Confirmed: Real Madrid midfield mainstay injured in national team training; will report back to club for tests International breaks often spell trouble for Real Madrid, especially when they leave key players injured at critical points in the season. Just days into the ongoing international break, Real Madrid received news of a major blow last night when Aurelien Tchouameni was said to have injured himself in training with the French national team. Having left training with discomfort, the midfielder was set to undergo tests to determine if his blow was major or minor, and whether or not he would continue with Zinedine Zidane’s side during this hiatus. The update is now in, and it is not one that will please Los Blancos . Injured again Indeed, confirmed for the French national team itself, Tchouameni has suffered a muscle injury, and the initial tests carried out by the national team medical staff rule out a minor blow. “Aurelien Tchouameni has sustained an injury to his right adductor muscle. “Following consultation with Real Madrid’s medical team, the French national team’s medical staff, in agreement with the player, have decided to release him back to his club. “He will not be replaced,” confirmed the statement. The player will thus leave the French national team and travel back to Madrid, where he will continue his recovery. The international break is over for him. Having suffered his blow early in the hiatus, the player will luckily have two free weeks to focus on his recovery before Real Madrid return to action. He will, however, undergo further tests in Madrid to determine his exact time out and the prognosis. A blow for Mourinho A big blow for Mourinho. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Injuries have not been kind to Tchouameni throughout his time at Real Madrid, with the player periodically suffering one or another physical setback. Most recently, the player suffered a blow after the FIFA World Cup and missed the opening phase of Real Madrid’s season under Jose Mourinho as well. He then slowly earned his place under the coach, proving himself to be a reliable physical presence in midfield. The Frenchman even struck up a good partnership with Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva and was close to earning an undisputed starter tag. The latest injury thus arrives as a setback to Mourinho’s plans, for the manager finally found a working midfield formula which is now in jeopardy. He will hope the player’s injury is only minor, but given that France have relieved him of duty, the chances are unlikely.

When the 22-year-old got in front of his marker to head in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys and put Club Brugge in front against PSV, he became the first German player to score five goals in a single Champions League campaign for a non-German club. The talented frontman is a German citizen, but was born in Italy, and Roberto Mancini has admitted he is trying to convince him to pledge his allegiance to the Azzurri. He's a strong, intelligent striker who can finish ruthlessly with both feet - a rare breed in the modern game - and the best is surely yet to come. McMahon was heralded for his great defense and ability to take advantage of the right field porch offensively in New York. Unfortunately, both failed him with woeful offense and disappointing defense in 2026. Yankees General Manager Brian Cashman was asked about McMahon’s role and revealed the following about third base: “We’ll look at it, without a doubt. We struggled there this year a little bit more than I would’ve expected. That doesn’t mean Ryan McMahon’s not capable of a lot more, too. We acquired him and he had a positive impact in 2025 when we got him. 2026 wasn’t the same follow-up. I know he’s capable of a lot more. So we’ll see how this shakes out but we’re open minded to see what we can do to improve the overall club. He’s signed through next year.” Cashman played both sides here by revealing he wants to see more from McMahon next season and discussing looking at all options. Tyler Kolek is no longer just making waves for his anti-Taylor Swift remark that got Swifties furious at the New York Knicks ’ third-string point guard. Kolek is also starting to be a legitimate and consistent rotation player for the Knicks. On Tuesday night, in a 117-85 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks, the 25-year-old point guard impressed yet again. Kolek, in just 15 minutes off the bench, scored 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting from the field. Miles McBride played more minutes than he did, but McBride is more of a combo guard anyway, with Kolek being more of a natural playmaker. And it looks as though Kolek has leapfrogged Jose Alvarado, who played just six minutes, in the rotation. Knicks head coach Mike Brown , of course, has never been shy to mix up his rotations. However, it’s important to note that Kolek was also playing key minutes for the Knicks earlier last season before he was gradually phased out of the rotation and relegated to garbage time duties in the playoffs.
